bug_semantics: llama.cpp DRY sampler stores caller-supplied dry_allowed_length as a signed int32 with no lower bound. An HTTP /v1/completions or /v1/chat/completions body can set dry_allowed_length to INT32_MIN; json_value copies that value into sampling params and llama_sampler_init_dry stores it unchanged. llama_sampler_dry_apply then (1) fails the last_n_repeat <= dry_allowed_length early-return because any token count is greater than INT32_MIN, (2) treats every repeat_len as eligible because repeat_len >= INT32_MIN is always true, and (3) computes int repeat_exp = repeat_len - dry_allowed_length, a signed integer underflow of INT32_MIN that is undefined in int32 and yields an out-of-range exponent used to mutate logits. Cyera/VulnCheck observed the resulting heap OOB read/underflow as SIGSEGV DoS or corrupted sampling probabilities. The same unbounded int is also accepted by --dry-allowed-length.
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism was first written when DRY sampling was added to llama.cpp (PR #9702). That change introduced llama_sampler_dry_apply's unguarded signed subtraction/comparisons on dry_allowed_length, stored the field without clamping in llama_sampler_init_dry_impl, parsed it from request JSON with json_value, and bound --dry-allowed-length from a raw int CLI callback. No later rewrite introduced the underflow; later commits only moved files (llama-sampling.cpp -> llama-sampler.cpp, server.cpp JSON parse -> server-task.cpp).

reasoning: CVE-2026-43628 is a real, published integer-underflow/OOB-read in ggml-org/llama.cpp's DRY sampler, not a withdrawn GHSA. The sink is llama_sampler_dry_apply's use of a signed dry_allowed_length that HTTP JSON can set to INT32_MIN because json_value and init_dry never reject negatives. git log -L :llama_sampler_dry_apply and parent-tree grep show those lines first appear in PR #9702. GitHub squash-merged that PR as ff252ea (b3978); protocol forbids using that squash as BIC. The four public PR members are in the clone; the first member 9697338 is the smallest surviving first-write, its parent 0a1c750 lacks the DRY field and apply function, and the three later members do not introduce the underflow. File renames and the server.cpp->server-task.cpp move carried the same unvalidated parse. Upstream later closed the disclosed HTTP path in e1efd0991/b9707 by hard-limiting dry_allowed_length to [0, INT32_MAX] on the completions schema used by both named endpoints, after the advisory window ending at b9058. AI authorship is judged only from the BIC commit object: human author wwoodsTM with human coauthors from the Kobold.cpp/l3utterfly port, no agent trailers, so NOT_AI.
